meta.title: Business Diagnostic — Know where your business stands
meta.description: The Forcelis Business Diagnostic is a structured analysis of your financial, commercial and operational performance: a Business Score, the findings that matter and a sequenced action plan. No system access required.

hero.title: Know where your business stands.
hero.subtitle: A structured analysis of your financial, commercial and operational performance — with the findings that matter and what to do about each one.

score.title: Forcelis Business Score
score.intro: Five dimensions on one scale, so they can be compared with each other and with the same company a period later. The score is the index into the report, not the report.
score.footnote: Scores shown are illustrative and do not describe any real company.

findings.title: What will we find?
findings.intro: Every finding names what was observed, why it matters and what to do. The four below are illustrative examples of the kind of finding the diagnostic produces.

items.title: Accounts receivable grew faster than revenue.
items.body: Collection is slowing relative to sales. The gap is financed by the company, and it never shows up in the income statement.
items.action: Review credit terms by customer segment and separate genuine disputes from routine late payment.

items.title: Customer concentration is a material commercial risk.
items.body: The top five customers account for a share of revenue at which losing one materially changes the year.
items.action: Quantify the exposure per customer and set a concentration target for the next four quarters.

items.title: Inventory turnover is below target.
items.body: A share of working capital is held in items that do not move at the rate the rest of the catalogue does.
items.action: Identify slow-moving items by value and decide, per item, whether to discount, return or stop reordering.

items.title: Gross margin fell in a key product category.
items.body: The decline is driven by input cost, not by price. It has been absorbed rather than passed through.
items.action: Compare purchase price movement against list price by category and decide where to reprice.

deliverables.title: A document your management team can work from.
deliverables.intro: Six sections, in the order a management team reads them. Written for the person who will not read the rest.

items.title: Financial analysis
items.body: Results, margins, costs and cash, restated in managerial terms with history.

items.title: Operational analysis
items.body: Inventory, purchasing, suppliers and the working capital they consume.

items.title: Key risks
items.body: What could damage the business, ordered by exposure.

items.title: Key opportunities
items.body: Where margin, cash or capacity is recoverable, with an estimated size.

items.title: Recommended actions
items.body: A short, sequenced list with an owner and a way to measure each one.

report.alt: Preview of the diagnostic report: a document with the overall score on its cover and the six sections listed as a table of contents.

process.title: Four steps.

steps.title: Scope
steps.body: A short call to understand the business, the period to analyze and the questions management already has.

steps.title: Send data
steps.body: Files you export from your own systems. Nothing is connected, nothing is installed.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.body: Ingestion, normalization and analysis on the platform, then review by the people who will present it.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: A working session on the findings and the recommended actions. The full document follows.

assurances: No tax portal or banking credentials, ever

inputs.title: What is needed from you
inputs.intro: The first item is the minimum. The rest deepen the analysis but are not required to start.

items.text: CFDI for the period — issued and received, including payment complements
Inventory report, if the business holds stock
Sales detail by customer and product, if kept outside invoicing

inputs.note: If something is missing, the affected metric is reported as unavailable with the reason. It is not estimated.

closing.title: Start with the diagnostic.
closing.body: It establishes the baseline. Everything after it — advisory, platform, managed services — is scoped from evidence rather than from a proposal.
